title: RESTful API Core Principles
summary: REST (Representational State Transfer) is an architectural style with key constraints like statelessness and uniform interface.

content.overview: REST architecture defines how networked applications should be designed around resources identified by URIs and manipulated through standard HTTP methods.
content.details: Core principles: Resources identified by URIs; Standard HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE); Stateless communication; Uniform interface.
content.examples: GET /users/123 retrieves user resource; POST /users creates a new user.
content.caveats: Statelessness means each request must contain all necessary context; server does not store client state between requests.
